item.description: Carry-On is a self-hosted tool for losing chat history and memory when you switch AI subscriptions: it aggregates conversations from ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini and exposes keyword search and retrieval through an MCP server. You can install it on HAOS in one click or deploy it with Docker, then add the custom MCP server to your current AI service. The author says existing options are either closed-source and paid or open-source but outdated.

item.title: [infoq] SvelteKit 3 进入 RC：svelte.config.js 没了，$lib 也要退休
item.description: The Svelte team has pushed SvelteKit 3 to release candidate, framing it as a cleanup rather than a feature release: svelte.config.js is removed and configuration now lives in vite.config.ts, while the $lib alias gives way to #lib built on Node subpath imports declared in package.json, which requires explicit file extensions. Svelte 5 is mandatory, migration runs via npx sv@next migrate sveltekit-3, and a stable release without further breaking changes is expected if testing goes well.

item.title: [hackernews] Fingerprints are the new cookies
item.description: This demo page fingerprints visitors without cookies: it derives a stable nickname from browser and device traits that survives clearing cookies or connecting through a VPN, and stays consistent in incognito until you switch devices. The author argues ad-funded sites running such scripts could link that identifier to your account data and sell it, undercutting the claim that the data is anonymized.

item.title: [infoq] Cursor 使用基于 S3 的 WAL，将 Git 存储扩展到每秒 300 多次 Push
item.description: Cursor has detailed Continuity, a Git storage architecture that treats a write-ahead log on S3 as the source of truth while local NVMe serves only as a warm cache, using Rendezvous Hashing and S3 atomic compare-and-swap so any node can accept pushes. In synthetic tests with S3 Express One Zone it handled over 300 pushes per second, with reads scaling linearly to 100 replicas. A commenter noted the figures haven't been independently verified.

item.title: [hackernews] The gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is widening
item.description: This Hacker News post dusts off an April tweet arguing that shared understanding of LLM capability has stopped being two groups talking past each other and become a sharp funnel. By rough napkin math, around 6 billion people, roughly 75% of the population, have barely come into contact with LLMs. It is aimed at anyone tracking the real reach of AI adoption.

It is the company's fourth round in six months, pushing its valuation from 10 billion to 15 billion RMB in three months. Engineers CJ Avilla and Harrison Stall described the mechanism at an AI Engineer New York 2026 workshop, aimed at developers building multi-agent systems.

item.description: xtool-org/xtool is a cross-platform replacement for Xcode: it builds a SwiftPM package into an iOS app, signs and installs it, and talks to Apple Developer Services programmatically from Linux, Windows, WSL or macOS. Aimed at developers who want iOS builds outside a Mac, or in CI, without depending on Xcode itself.

item.title: [github_trending] lyogavin/airllm
item.description: AirLLM cuts inference memory enough to run a 70B model on a single 4GB GPU without quantization, distillation or pruning. Its README claims Kimi K3 (2.8T) fits under 4GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) on 6GB and DeepSeek-V3 (671B) on roughly 12GB, with new support for training large models on small VRAM. Aimed at developers short on GPU memory.

item.title: [github_trending] mksglu/context-mode
item.description: Context Mode is an optimization layer for AI coding agents that sandboxes tool output, which it says cuts context usage by 98%, persists session memory, and enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP plus hooks. It ships as an npm package under the ELv2 license, aimed at developers whose agents keep blowing through their context window.

item.title: [github_trending] vercel-labs/skills
item.description: vercel-labs/skills is Vercel Labs' CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem, runnable through npx skills. It lists support for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 75 more agents, giving developers a single command-line entry point instead of a separate setup per tool, which helps anyone juggling multiple coding agents.
